summary.tldr: Requires courts to consider electronic monitoring for some accused charged with intimate partner offences and adds judge training on intimate partner violence and coercive control.
what_it_does: Requires a justice, before making a release order for an accused charged with an offence against an intimate partner, to consider whether electronic monitoring should be a condition for safety and security.
Adds electronic monitoring as a possible release condition when the Attorney General asks for it.
Updates the list of offences for release conditions to cover violence used, threatened or attempted against the accused’s intimate partner.

Requires the Canadian Judicial Council to hold continuing education seminars for judges on intimate partner violence, coercive control, sexual assault law, and social context, including systemic racism and discrimination.
Requires the Council to report each year to the Minister on those seminars within 60 days after the end of the calendar year.
who_it_affects: Accused persons charged with intimate partner offences
summary.background: The bill changes release order rules in the Criminal Code and judicial education rules in the Judges Act.
